p.src: Now the Great Sage Sun, together with Bajie and Sha Seng, took leave of Old Chen and came to the riverbank. He said, “Brothers, decide between you: which of you will enter the water first?” Bajie said, “Brother, neither of us is especially capable. You had better enter the water first.” Pilgrim said, “I will tell you frankly, worthy brothers: if the demon were in the mountains, you would not need to exert yourselves at all; but when it comes to affairs beneath the water, I cannot go. Even to enter a sea or travel along a river, I must form the water-repelling spell with my fingers, or transform myself into some fish or crab, before I can go. But while forming such a spell, I cannot swing my iron staff, exercise my divine powers, or fight a demon. I have long known that both of you are accustomed to the water, and that is why I want you to go down.” Sha Seng said, “Brother, though I can go down, I do not know what lies on the riverbed. Let us all go together. Elder Brother, transform yourself into something, or let me carry you. We shall part the waters and seek out the demon’s lair, and you can go inside first to investigate. If Master is still there and has suffered no harm, we can put forth all our strength in battle; but if this was not the monster’s doing, or if Master has drowned or been eaten by a demon, there will be no need for us to search in vain, and we can promptly seek another road. What do you think?” Pilgrim said, “Your words are reasonable, worthy brother. Which of you will carry me?” Bajie secretly rejoiced, thinking, “That monkey has played more tricks on me than I can count. Now it turns out that he cannot manage in water. Let old Hog carry him and play a trick on him for once.” The fool called out with a broad grin, “Brother, I will carry you.” Pilgrim knew at once what he intended, but decided to turn the scheme to his own advantage. “Yes, very well,” he said. “You have somewhat more strength than Wujing.” Bajie then took him upon his back.

p.src: Sha Seng opened a path through the water, and the brothers entered the River of Heaven together. After they had travelled a hundred or so li along the riverbed, the fool decided to play a trick on Pilgrim. Pilgrim immediately plucked out a hair, transformed it into a false body, and laid it across Bajie’s back; his true body changed into a hog louse and clung tightly inside Bajie’s ear. As Bajie walked on, he suddenly pretended to stumble and deliberately flung Pilgrim forward, sending him tumbling to the ground with a thud. But that false body had been transformed from a hair, so it simply drifted away and vanished without a trace. Sha Seng said, “Second Brother, what do you think you are doing? It would be one thing if you merely failed to watch your step and fell in the mud yourself, but now you have thrown Elder Brother somewhere, and we do not even know where he has gone.” Bajie said, “That monkey could not withstand a fall; one tumble and he dissolved away. Brother, never mind whether he is alive or dead. Let you and me go and look for Master first.” Sha Seng said, “That will not do. We still need him. Though he knows nothing of watercraft, he is cleverer than we are. If he does not come, I will not go with you.” From inside Bajie’s ear, Pilgrim could contain himself no longer and shouted, “Wujing, old Sun is right here!” When Sha Seng heard him, he laughed and said, “Enough! This fool is doomed. How could you dare play a trick on him? Now we can hear your voice but cannot see you. What are we to do?” Bajie was so frightened that he knelt in the mud and kowtowed, saying, “Brother, I was in the wrong. Once we have rescued Master, I will apologize properly on shore. Where are you speaking from? You are frightening me to death! Please show yourself in your true form. I will carry you and never again dare offend you.” Pilgrim said, “You are still carrying me. I will not torment you. Hurry on, hurry on.” The fool kept muttering apology after apology, then scrambled up and continued onward with Sha Seng.

p.src: After travelling another hundred or so li, they suddenly looked up and saw a many-storied residence. Above it were four large characters: “Mansion of the Water Turtle.” Sha Seng said, “This must be the demon’s dwelling. Since the two of us know nothing of its true strength, how can we go to the gate and challenge it?” Pilgrim said, “Wujing, is there water inside or outside that gate?” Sha Seng said, “There is none.” Pilgrim said, “Since there is no water, conceal yourselves nearby while old Sun goes to investigate.”

p.src: The splendid Great Sage crawled out of Bajie’s ear, shook himself, and transformed into a long-legged prawn. With two or three bounds, he leapt through the gate. Opening his eyes to look, he saw the monster seated above, with the various aquatic creatures arrayed on either side. A mottled mandarin-fish crone sat at one side, and they were all discussing how to eat the Tang Monk. Pilgrim searched carefully on both sides but could not find him. Suddenly he saw a large-bellied prawn crone approaching, who went straight to the western gallery and stopped there. Pilgrim hopped before her and addressed her, saying, “Granny, the king and the others are discussing how to eat the Tang Monk, but where is the Tang Monk?” The prawn crone said, “The king brought down snow and froze the river to capture the Tang Monk, and yesterday he placed him inside a stone chest behind the palace. We are merely waiting until tomorrow. If his disciples do not come to make trouble, we shall strike up the music and feast upon him.”

p.src: Pilgrim could restrain himself no longer and cried, “Master, do not resent this watery calamity. The scripture says, ‘Earth is the mother of the Five Elements, and water is the source of the Five Elements. Without earth nothing is born; without water nothing grows.’ Old Sun has come.” On hearing him, Tripitaka said, “Disciple, save me!” Pilgrim said, “Set your mind at ease for now. Once we have captured the demon, I promise you will be delivered from this ordeal.” Tripitaka said, “Make haste and act! If I remain here another day, I shall surely suffocate to death.” Pilgrim said, “It will be all right, it will be all right. I am off!”

p.src: He hurriedly turned back and leapt outside. Beyond the gate he resumed his true form and called, “Bajie!” The fool and Sha Seng came forward and asked, “Brother, how did it go?” Pilgrim said, “It was indeed this monster who deceived and captured Master. Master has suffered no harm; the monster has confined him beneath a stone chest. You two must challenge it at once, while old Sun returns to the surface first. If you can capture it, do so; if you cannot, pretend to be defeated and lure it out of the water, and I will strike it down.” Sha Seng said, “Go on ahead without concern, Brother. We shall judge the situation and act accordingly.” Pilgrim formed the water-repelling spell with his fingers, bored his way out of the river, and stood waiting on the bank. Of him we speak no more for now.

p.src: The fiend came out through the gate, followed by a hundred or so lesser demons, each brandishing spear or sword as they formed two ranks. He said to Bajie, “Are you a monk from that temple? Why have you come here making such a clamor?” Bajie shouted, “You insolent wretch who refuses to die! You traded insults with me the night before last; why pretend today not to know me and ask who I am? I am a disciple of the holy monk from the Great Tang in the Eastern Land, journeying to the Western Heaven to worship the Buddha and seek the scriptures. You play your tricks and falsely style yourself the Great King of Numinous Power, demanding boys and girls to devour in Chen Family Village. I was the ‘Gold by the Catty’ from Chen Qing’s household. Do you not recognize me?” The monster said, “You monk are utterly unreasonable. By transforming yourself into Gold by the Catty, you committed the crime of impersonation. Far from eating you, I had the back of my hand wounded by you. I already let you off for that, so why have you come seeking trouble at my very door?” Bajie said, “If you let me off, why did you then summon a cold wind and heavy snow, freeze the river solid, and harm my master? Bring my master out at once, and the whole affair will be at an end; but let so much as half a ‘no’ pass your teeth, and you shall taste the rake in my hand—I will show you no mercy.” Hearing this, the fiend gave a faint, cold laugh. “This monk wags his tongue and boasts outrageously. Indeed, it was I who made the cold and snow, froze the river, and seized your master. Now you have come clamoring at my gate, thinking to reclaim him, but I fear this time will be unlike the last. Then I was attending a feast and had brought no weapon, so you wounded me by chance; now do not think of leaving until you have fought me for three rounds. If you can withstand me for three rounds, I shall return your master; if you cannot, I shall eat you along with him.”

p.src: The three fought beneath the water for four hours without either side gaining the advantage. Zhu Bajie realized they could not defeat him and winked at Monk Sha. The two feigned defeat and, trailing their weapons, turned and fled. The monster ordered, “Little ones, hold your positions here while I chase down those rogues, capture them, and bring them back to make up a feast for you!” See how he drove the two of them out of the water like wind sweeping fallen leaves or rain beating withered blossoms.

p.src: The Great Sage Sun stood on the eastern bank, staring unblinkingly at the movement of the water by the riverbank. Suddenly the waves began to churn and shouts and roars rang out. Bajie was first to leap ashore, crying, “He is coming! He is coming!” Monk Sha also reached the bank and cried, “He is coming! He is coming!” The fiend followed after them, shouting, “Where do you think you are going?” The moment his head emerged, the Pilgrim shouted, “Watch my staff!” The fiend twisted aside to evade the blow, then hurriedly raised his bronze hammer to block and retaliate. One churned up waves beside the river, while the other displayed his might upon the bank. Before they had exchanged three rounds, the fiend could no longer parry. He made a feint, plunged back into the water, and at once the wind subsided and the waves grew still.

p.src: The Pilgrim returned to the high cliff and said, “Brothers, you have worked hard.” Monk Sha said, “Brother, that fiend is clearly no match for you on land, but beneath the water he is formidable indeed. Second Brother and I attacked him together from both sides, yet could only fight him to a draw. What are we to do now to rescue Master?” The Pilgrim said, “We must not hesitate, lest he harm Master.” Bajie said, “Brother, I shall go down and lure him out again. Say nothing, but wait in midair. As soon as you judge that his head has emerged, bring your staff straight down like a pestle pounding garlic and land one solid blow squarely on his crown. Even if it does not kill him, it will surely leave him clutching his head and reeling. Then Old Zhu will catch him with a rake and settle his account for good.” The Pilgrim said, “Exactly, exactly! This is called ‘an attack coordinated from within and without,’ and only thus can we succeed.” The two of them then entered the water again; of this no more need be said for the moment.

p.src: Now the fiend, having escaped alive from his defeat, returned to his residence. The lesser demons received him into the palace, and the old mandarin-fish dame stepped forward to ask, “Great King, how far did you chase those two monks?” The fiend said, “It turned out that those monks had another helper. When the two leapt ashore, that helper swung an iron staff at me. I dodged it and fought him. I do not know how many catties that staff of his weighs, but my bronze hammer could never withstand it. Before we had fought three rounds, I was defeated and came back.” The old mandarin-fish dame said, “Great King, do you remember what that helper looked like?” The fiend said, “He was a monk with a hairy face, a thunder-god’s beak, pointed ears, a flattened nose, and fiery eyes with golden pupils.” Hearing this, the old mandarin-fish dame shuddered and said, “Great King, fortunately you knew when to retreat and escaped with your life; had you fought another three rounds, you certainly would not have survived intact. I know that monk.” The fiend said, “Who is he, then?” The old mandarin-fish dame said, “Years ago, in the Eastern Ocean, I heard the old Dragon King speak of his renown. He is the Handsome Monkey King, the Great Sage Equaling Heaven—the Supreme Immortal of the Grand Unity in the Upper Realm, born of the primal, undivided breath—who caused havoc in Heaven five hundred years ago. Now he has embraced Buddhism and protects the Tang Monk on his journey to the Western Heaven for scriptures; he has taken the name Sun Wukong, the Pilgrim. His divine powers are immense and his transformations countless. Great King, why did you provoke him? From now on, you must never fight him again.”

Hearing this, the old mandarin-fish dame shuddered and said, “Great King, fortunately you knew when to retreat and escaped with your life;
had you fought another three rounds, you certainly would not have survived intact.
I know that monk.”
The fiend said, “Who is he, then?”

The old mandarin-fish dame said, “Years ago, in the Eastern Ocean, I heard the old Dragon King speak of his renown. He is the Handsome Monkey King, the Great Sage Equaling Heaven—the Supreme Immortal of the Grand Unity in the Upper Realm, born of the primal, undivided breath—who caused havoc in Heaven five hundred years ago.

ja: そんごくうぎょうじゃ
u.src: Now he has embraced Buddhism and protects the Tang Monk on his journey to the Western Heaven for scriptures; he has taken the name Sun Wukong, the Pilgrim.
His divine powers are immense and his transformations countless. Great King, why did you provoke him?
From now on, you must never fight him again.”

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, a little demon came in through the gate and reported, “Your Majesty, those two monks have come back to the gate to challenge us.” The demon said, “My worthy sister’s counsel is far-sighted. We shall not go out again and will see what they do.” He hurriedly gave the order: “Little ones, shut the gate tight. As the saying goes, ‘Let them shout outside the gate as they please; we simply will not open it.’ Let them pester us for two days. When their ardor has cooled and they go away, can we not enjoy Tang Monk at our leisure?” All the little demons moved stones and packed in clods of earth, sealing the gate completely.

Seeing this, Sha Monk said, “Second Brother, this monster is utterly terrified and refuses to come out. Let us return to the riverbank and discuss with Elder Brother what to do.” Bajie agreed, and they went straight back to the eastern bank.

p.src: The Great Sage swiftly mounted an auspicious radiance, left the river mouth behind, and headed straight for the Southern Sea. In less than half an hour, he saw Mount Luojia already close at hand. He lowered his cloud and went directly to Potalaka Cliff. The devas of the twenty-four divisions, the Great Guardian of the Mountain, the pilgrim Moksha, the Boy Sudhana, and the Dragon Girl Who Holds the Pearl all came forward together, greeted him with bows, and asked, “What brings the Great Sage here?” The Pilgrim replied, “I have business on which I must see the Bodhisattva.” The deities said, “The Bodhisattva left her cave this morning, permitted no one to accompany her, and went alone into the bamboo grove to enjoy the scenery. Please sit for a while before the Emerald Cliff and wait for the Bodhisattva to emerge.”

p.src: In moments they arrived in the region of the River That Reaches Heaven. When Bajie and Sha Monk saw them, they said, “Elder Brother is so impatient that heaven knows how he shouted and made a scene at the Southern Sea, forcing the Bodhisattva to come before she had even dressed herself.” Before they had finished speaking, the Bodhisattva reached the riverbank. The two bowed down and said, “Bodhisattva, forgive us for troubling you without leave. We have sinned, we have sinned.” The Bodhisattva untied a silk cord from around her robe and fastened it securely to the basket. Holding the cord, she stood with one foot upon a cloud, cast the basket into the river, and dragged it upstream while chanting, “Let the dead depart and the living remain. Let the dead depart and the living remain!” After chanting it seven times, she raised the basket. There inside was a gleaming golden fish, still blinking its eyes and moving its scales. The Bodhisattva called, “Wukong, hurry into the water and save your master.” The Pilgrim said, “How can I rescue Master when the fiend has not yet been caught?” The Bodhisattva said, “Is he not here in this basket?” Bajie and Sha Monk bowed and asked, “How did this fish acquire such powers?” The Bodhisattva said, “He was originally a goldfish raised in my lotus pond. Each day he floated to the surface to listen to the scriptures and thereby cultivated his powers. That nine-petaled bronze hammer was an unopened lotus bud which he refined into a weapon. I do not know on what day a high tide arose and he escaped to this place. This morning, as I leaned on the railing to view the flowers, I noticed that the wretch did not come out to pay his respects. Counting on my fingers and tracing the signs, I calculated that he had become a monster here and was harming your master. Therefore, without even taking time to dress myself, I exercised my divine skill and wove this bamboo basket to capture him.”

p.src: The Pilgrim said, “Bodhisattva, since that is so, please wait a moment while we summon all the faithful people of Chen Family Village to behold your gracious countenance: first, that your blessing may remain with them; and second, that by telling them how you subdued this monster, we may teach mortals to believe and make offerings.” The Bodhisattva said, “Very well. p.src: Bajie and Sha Monk parted the waters and went straight to the Turtle Mansion to search for their master. Inside, they found that all the aquatic monsters and fish spirits had perished and were rotting away. They entered the rear palace, opened the stone chest, took Tang Monk upon their backs, and emerged from the waves to rejoin the others. The brothers Chen Qing kowtowed in gratitude, saying, “Reverend sirs, you would not heed our pleas that you remain, and so you have suffered all this hardship.” Pilgrim said, “There is no need to speak of it. From next year onward, the households here will no longer need to hold sacrificial rites. That king has now been utterly destroyed and will never harm you again. Old Chen, now I really must trouble you: quickly find us a boat and ferry us across the river.” Chen Qing replied, “Yes, certainly, certainly.” He immediately ordered planks to be taken apart and fashioned into a boat. When the villagers heard this, every one of them gladly offered to contribute. One said, “I shall buy the mast and sail.” Another said, “I shall provide the poles and oars.” Some said, “I shall supply the ropes.” Others said, “I shall hire the boatmen.”

p.src: The old turtle called again, “Great Sage, do not build a boat. I shall carry you, master and disciples, across.” Pilgrim brandished his iron staff and cried, “You accursed beast! If you come near the bank, I shall kill you with one blow.” The old turtle said, “I am grateful for the Great Sage’s kindness and sincerely wish to carry you and your master across. Why do you mean to strike me instead?” Pilgrim asked, “What kindness have I ever shown you?” The old turtle replied, “Great Sage, you do not know that the Turtle Mansion beneath these waters is my home, handed down through my family from generation to generation. After awakening to my original nature and nurturing spiritual vitality, I cultivated the Way here. I rebuilt my ancestral dwelling throughout and established it as the Turtle Mansion. Nine years ago, during a sea surge that churned the waves, that fiend rode the tide here. Trusting in his savage might, he fought me, injured many of my children, and seized many of my kin. I was no match for him, and he took possession of my lair for nothing. Now the Great Sage has come to rescue Master Tang, invited Bodhisattva Guanyin to cleanse away the evil miasma, and had the monster taken away, restoring the mansion to me. Now my whole family is reunited; no longer must we endure mud and earth, but may dwell once more in our old home. This kindness is weightier than the hills and deeper than the sea. And it is not only we who have benefited. The people of this village are freed from their yearly sacrifices, and the sons and daughters of countless households have been saved. This truly is a kindness that has achieved two benefits with a single deed. How could I dare not repay it?” Hearing this, Pilgrim was secretly delighted. He put away his iron staff and asked, “Are these truly your sincere feelings?” The old turtle replied, “The Great Sage’s grace is so vast and profound—how would I dare utter falsehoods?” Pilgrim said, “If you are sincere, swear an oath to Heaven.” The old turtle opened his red mouth and swore to Heaven: “If I am not sincere in carrying Tang Monk across the River That Reaches Heaven, may my body dissolve into blood.” Pilgrim laughed and said, “Come ashore, then! Come ashore!”

p.src: When they reached the riverbank, every man and woman, old and young, of Chen Family Village came to bow and see them off. Pilgrim had the horse led onto the white turtle’s shell. He asked Tang Monk to stand to the left of the horse’s neck, Sha Monk to the right, Bajie behind the horse, while he himself stood in front. Still fearing that the turtle might misbehave, he untied his tiger-sinew sash, threaded it through the old turtle’s nostrils, and drew it up like a bridle. He planted one foot upon the shell and the other upon its head; in one hand he held his iron staff, and with the other he pulled the bridle. He called, “Old turtle, go slowly! If you tilt even a little, you will get a blow on the head.” The old turtle said, “I would not dare, I would not dare.” Then he stretched out his four legs and trod the water as though walking on level ground. Everyone on the bank burned incense and kowtowed, chanting, “Namo Amitabha Buddha.” Truly it was this: real arhats had descended to the mortal world, and living bodhisattvas had appeared. The people continued bowing until the travelers vanished from sight, and only then returned home. Of them we speak no more.

p.src: Now the master rode upon the white turtle, and in less than a day they crossed all eight hundred li of the River That Reaches Heaven and stepped ashore with hands and feet perfectly dry. Tripitaka climbed the bank, joined his palms, and thanked him: “Old turtle, you have taken great trouble for us. I have nothing to give you, but when I return with the scriptures, I shall repay your kindness.” The old turtle said, “There is no need for you to bestow any reward, Master. I have heard that the Buddha in the Western Heaven is beyond birth and extinction and knows the affairs of both past and future. I have cultivated myself here for more than thirteen hundred years. Though my life has been prolonged, my body made light, and I have learned human speech, I still cannot shed my original shell. I earnestly beg you, venerable master, when you reach the Western Heaven, to ask the Buddha when I may shed this shell and whether I may obtain a human body.” Tripitaka readily promised, “I shall ask, I shall ask.” Only then did the old turtle plunge into the water and depart.

u.src: Now the master rode upon the white turtle, and in less than a day they crossed all eight hundred li of the River That Reaches Heaven and stepped ashore with hands and feet perfectly dry.

Tripitaka climbed the bank, joined his palms, and thanked him: “Old turtle, you have taken great trouble for us. I have nothing to give you, but when I return with the scriptures, I shall repay your kindness.”
The old turtle said, “There is no need for you to bestow any reward, Master.
I have heard that the Buddha in the Western Heaven is beyond birth and extinction and knows the affairs of both past and future.

ja: せんさんびゃくよねん
u.src: I have cultivated myself here for more than thirteen hundred years. Though my life has been prolonged, my body made light, and I have learned human speech, I still cannot shed my original shell.
I earnestly beg you, venerable master, when you reach the Western Heaven, to ask the Buddha when I may shed this shell and whether I may obtain a human body.”
Tripitaka readily promised, “I shall ask, I shall ask.”
Only then did the old turtle plunge into the water and depart.

p.src: Pilgrim then helped Tang Monk mount his horse. Bajie shouldered the luggage, Sha Monk attended close beside them, and the master and disciples found the main road and continued straight westward. And so it was:

u.src: Pilgrim then helped Tang Monk mount his horse. Bajie shouldered the luggage, Sha Monk attended close beside them, and the master and disciples found the main road and continued straight westward.
And so it was:

p.src: After all, how much farther they had to travel and what good or ill fortune still awaited them is unknown; listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
